title: "003 — Timeline UX fixes"

## 003 — Timeline UX fixes {#sec-003}

> **Status:** standing

**Goal.** Fix four defects reported against the freshly shipped timeline: (1) the orbit
spinner spun forever on finished replies, persisting after reload; (2) turn order rendered
the reply before its thought process, violating canonical chronological order — reasoning,
then assistant text, then tool activity; (3) terminal tools such as the choices presenter
ended the turn by design yet displayed a failure icon and "No Result Recorded"; (4) the
diagnostics panel crashed whenever an MCP server connected and disconnected in one
session, blocking users from opening chats at all. Each fix ships with a regression test
that fails without it.

**Why.** These were the first real-world verdicts on the kind registry. The permanent
spinner trained users to ignore genuine progress signals. Misordered renders read as
dishonest history — the exact failure mode the kind model was built to eliminate. And the
diagnostics crash took priority purely operationally: it destroyed the reporting channel
the other three bugs depended on.

**Outcome & reversals.** All four landed as presentation-layer surgery plus one
persist-order correction, with no schema change and golden provider-context tests passing
unmodified. Root-causing the third defect revealed deeper rot: the agent loop persisted
tool iterations out of order, and worse, the tool-pairing map was keyed by row id instead
of tool-call id — meaning **no production tool pair had ever grouped**, invisible because
test fixtures set both fields to identical strings. The fixes: persist reasoning first per
iteration; key pairing correctly; drop the end-of-timeline flush that fabricated false
chronology; add a stable within-turn reorder pass that repairs wrongly-stored history
without touching stored data. Later features extended this work:
[#004](004-internal-area-unification.qmd#sec-004) taught awaiting-approval calls to read as pending rather than failed, and
[#005](005-shape-driven-results.qmd#sec-005) rebuilt the expanded result body.

**Learnings.**

- Never let fixture identifiers equal their join keys — synthetic equality masked a
  production-wide pairing failure.
- Pair a presentation-time repair pass (fixes historical display without data writes) with
  persist-order fixes (stop manufacturing bad history going forward).
- Classification belongs to one registry; a UI-maintained tool-name list drifts the moment
  the backend changes.
- Availability of the bug-reporting path ranks above UX polish in triage.
